note: The six questions and answer matrix summarise the published evidence. tools/verify.py --matrix checks each cell against the published files. Notes cite source documents, not speakers; personal names and proponent organisations are not rendered.

approaches.label: Catalog-first
approaches.one_line: The rule is a catalog control; the check is a software component in a component definition.

approaches.label: Component-first
approaches.one_line: The rule uses a proposed assembly on the product component; the check uses a proposed assembly on a validation component.

approaches.label: Assessment-first
approaches.one_line: The rule is an assessment plan activity or step; a property identifies the check.

empty_states.label: Unanswered, no stated position
empty_states.rendering: hollow with a light dotted fill
empty_states.meaning: The published content does not answer the question or state a reason for the omission.

slots.name: What the rule requires
slots.question: What condition must hold, and where is the requirement defined?
slots.why_separate: A technology-specific requirement defines one testable condition. Under pre-read settled item 7, the rule definition declares parameter options and a default.

slots.name: How the rule links to a control
slots.question: Does this rule help satisfy a regulatory control, and which one?
slots.why_separate: A rule is finer-grained than a control and may serve several controls, one, or none. A control-linking mechanism is required, but using the mechanism is optional.

binding_times.label: Author-time, inline
binding_times.mechanism: The rule declares its control directly

binding_times.label: Author-time, by pointer
binding_times.mechanism: A prop carries an external framework identifier that a consumer must resolve

binding_times.label: Late, external
binding_times.mechanism: A separate artifact links a rule to a control after publication
binding_times.why: mapping-item.type is restricted by allOf to control and statement, and mapping-item has neither uuid nor href. External mappings therefore reach rules modelled as controls or control statements, not component rules or activities. This OSCAL schema constraint does not establish a preferred approach.

cost_of_leaving_empty.observation: Available. AR observation requires only uuid, description, methods and collected, with no control reference.
cost_of_leaving_empty.finding: Not available. finding requires target; finding-target requires type, restricted by allOf to statement-id or objective-id, both control-derived.
cost_of_leaving_empty.summary: Without a control link, an assessor can record an observation but not a finding against a control statement or objective.

slots.name: How the rule is tested
slots.question: Which executable or procedure tests the rule?
slots.why_separate: A rule may have several checks, one per tool. Pre-read settled item 4 keeps executables outside OSCAL and references them. Settled item 5 separates rules from checks.

slots.name: What the check runs against
slots.question: Is the subject a host, component, account or another resource?
slots.why_separate: The subject identifies the assessed host, inventory item, component or account. Criterion 8 addresses response fidelity.
slots.not_established_note: Evidence register item 8: authoritative semantics for assessment platform versus asset versus component were to be posted to the NIST OSCAL team on 17 July. No response is in the record.

slots.name: What performs the check
slots.question: Which tool or person performs the check, and how is the runner identified?
slots.why_separate: The runner may be a validation component, assessment platform, tool or person. The method prop identifies examine, interview or test.
slots.not_established_note: Same as question 4. Three approaches use six different subsets of assessment-assets, assessment-platforms, uses-components, validation components, origin actors, task-level props and the method prop.

slots.name: How the system claims it meets the rule
slots.question: How does the system owner describe implementation of the rule?
slots.why_separate: The system owner provides a narrative claim of implementation and design intent per component. The SSP represents claims through implemented-requirement, statement and by-component.

slots.name: How an assessment records the outcome
slots.question: Was the rule satisfied, when, and for which subject?
slots.why_separate: The assessor records evidence and a binary or graded outcome per subject at a point in time. The AR uses observation, finding and status. A desired-state rule has a binary satisfaction condition; the SSP implementation claim is narrative.

matrix.note: One control per rule. Existing assemblies capture context around the rule's intent.
The proposed rules assembly sits on the component alongside control-implementations.
The activity defines the rule and the step describes the check. Without a parameter field, required values are recorded in text.
A separate mapping collection links rules to framework controls. The published corpus contains no such mapping document.
Existing assemblies link the component to the control. Linking an individual rule requires the proposed assembly.
Two levels: reviewed-controls defines the required plan scope; related-controls optionally links an activity to controls.
The check identifier resolves within the runtime to an executable machine check.
The proposed schema places both composite-key fields on the check. The rule has no reference back to the check.
Three conventions: CISA references an executable through a JSON string in a prop; STIG and CIS describe checks in prose.
The by-component response identifies a component, not an instance. An assessment plan cannot import a catalog directly.
The proposed rule reference extends by-component. An assessor can include the component definition and associated checks in an assessment plan.
The plan defines subject scope; activity-associated tasks select targets. Both can identify inventory items, representing instances rather than classes.
The content records inputs and outputs but not the engine. ConfigRuleId resolves within the engine. No assessor workflow is shown; an assessment plan cannot import a catalog directly.
The proposed schema records four open questions about runners, including how an assessment asset links to a task.
The platform executes the check, a referenced component represents the plugin, and a task property identifies the platform.
The component definition describes how a component could satisfy a control, not a system's implementation. The corpus contains no system security plan.
The claim uses a by-component response. Identifying the supporting rule requires the proposed implementing-rules assembly.
The assessment plan references the document containing the implementation claim. A back-matter resource supports cases without a plan of record.
The repository documentation lists compliance validation automation as a future consideration; no assessment results are published.
The result contains observations but no findings or objective status. The control reference must be recovered through the assessment plan.
A separate results document imports the plan. Findings have targets and status; observations identify the executed activity as the subject.

finding: Questions 1 and 2 are answered by all three approaches. No approach fully answers both 6a and 6b, and no approach answers every question.

answer_states.label: Answered
answer_states.meaning: The published content answers this question.

answer_states.label: Partly answered
answer_states.meaning: The published content answers part of this question.

answer_states.label: Not answered
answer_states.meaning: The published content does not answer the question or state a reason for the omission.

mechanism_states.label: Released OSCAL assembly
mechanism_states.meaning: A released OSCAL assembly provides the capability without a schema change.

mechanism_states.label: Proposed assembly
mechanism_states.meaning: The capability requires a proposed assembly. Interoperable use requires schema adoption and tool support for the new structure.

mechanism_states.label: Namespaced property
mechanism_states.meaning: A property in the publisher's namespace provides the capability. Tools need a shared convention to interpret the property; the OSCAL schema does not define the meaning.

legend.label: How to read an answer
legend.why_one_block: Each cell combines an answer state with mechanism badges. A shared legend explains both dimensions together.
legend.why_uneven: Answer states describe evidence coverage. Mechanism descriptions also explain schema and tool-support requirements, so the descriptions need additional detail.

mechanism_note: Answer states describe coverage in the published corpus. Mechanism badges identify the OSCAL structures needed to represent an answer. Evidence coverage does not establish schema adoption or tool interoperability.
carrier_note: Each answer identifies the OSCAL model and assemblies representing the capability. Rules use catalog controls, component rules or assessment activities; the choice affects references to checks, claims and results.
paths_note: Each runner path shows one input document and one output document. The documents depend on whether the system owner or assessor runs the check.
